short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.say: New LED! Let's connect it straight to my 9 V battery!
short_scenes.narration: This is Volt. He just bought a shiny new LED, and he connects it straight to a nine volt battery.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Watch the current rush through. Way too much! The LED flashes, and pop, it's burnt. Volt has no idea why.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Here's the problem. Nothing in the circuit was controlling the current. An LED only wants about twenty milliamps.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Now he adds a resistor in the path. Look at the meter: just twenty milliamps. The LED glows bright and safe.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: The resistor limits the current. The LED uses about two volts, so the resistor takes the other seven: seven divided by twenty milliamps gives three hundred and fifty ohms.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.say: Watch the full Resistor video on our channel!
short_scenes.narration: For the detailed explanation, watch the full video on our channel. It's part of our complete Network Theory course.
